title: Cheng Han
capsule: Cheng Han was the first of the Sixteen Kingdoms to be formally established, founded in 306 by Li Xiong of the Ba-Di people after a refugee crisis drove tens of thousands from Guanzhong into Sichuan in the aftermath of the War of the Eight Princes. Li Xiong (r. 306–334), having already taken Chengdu in 304, proclaimed the kingdom of Cheng; it was renamed Han by Li Shou in 338. The polity controlled the Chengdu plain and surrounding Sichuan commanderies, benefiting from the region's agricultural richness and geographic isolation. Li Shou's son Li Shi proved unable to maintain order, and Eastern Jin general Huan Wen invaded from the east in 347, capturing Chengdu and extinguishing the dynasty.
